name: Lower Chulym Turkic
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Pomorska, Marzanna 2001. The Chulyms and Their Language: An Attempt at a Description of Chulym Phonetics and Nominal Morphology. Turk Dilleri Arastirmalari 11.
earlier_scan.note: Phonetics description exists but no online full text located

new_statements.quote: Ударение слова в целом тяготеет к конечному слогу, однако в формах слов с узким конечным гласным ударение смещается на предыдущий широкий гласный: парча ‘весь; все’; парчаларда ‘во всех; везде’; парчозун ‘(вижу его / их) весь’; парчалорунда ‘во всех (их); везде’.
new_statements.translation: Word stress on the whole gravitates to the final syllable; however, in word forms with a narrow (high) final vowel the stress shifts to the preceding broad (non-high) vowel: parča 'all; everyone'; parčalarda 'in all; everywhere'; parčozun '(I see him/them) all'; parčalorunda 'in all (of them); everywhere'.
new_statements.citation: Kondiyakov, A. F. & V. M. Lemskaya. 2021. Chulymskij jazyk d. Pasechnoe Tjukhtetskogo rajona Krasnojarskogo kraja 2007-2021 gg. Tom I: Slovar', formy slov i grammaticheskie primery. Tomsk: Izdatel'stvo Tomskogo universiteta (sci. ed. A. V. Dybo).
new_statements.locator: Part I, Vvedenie, 'Fonologicheskaja sistema glasnykh meletskogo govora srednechulymskogo dialekta', p. 23 (PDF p. 25); repeated verbatim in Tom II p. 8 (PDF p. 10)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE:, PDF p. 25 = printed p. 23, section 'Fonologicheskaja sistema glasnykh meletskogo govora srednechulymskogo dialekta', text layer via extracted text reads exactly: "Ударение слова в целом тяготеет к конечному слогу, однако в формах слов с узким конечным гласным ударение смещается на предыдущий широкий гласный: парча ‘весь; все’; парчаларда ‘во всех; везде’; парчозун ‘(вижу его / их) весь’; парчалорунда ‘во всех (их); везде’." — identical to the reported quote. The Tom II copy ( PDF p. 10 = printed p. 8) is the same rule but NOT strictly verbatim: 'к последнему слогу' for 'к конечному слогу' and different gloss punctuation ("парча ‘весь’; ‘все’... парчозун (вижу его / их) ‘весь’"). The…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default final-syllable stress; if the last syllable contains a high ('narrow') vowel, stress retracts to the nearest preceding syllable with a non-high ('broad') vowel. A vowel-quality-sensitive coding (default-final, high vowels skipped) would also be defensible.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the high-final-vowel retraction; the hedge 'в целом' (on the whole) signals a tendency rather than an exceptionless rule. No statement about loanwords or suffix classes.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; stated for inflected word forms (case/possessive forms) of the Melet subdialect of Middle Chulym as spoken by A. F. Kondiyakov (Pasechnoe, Krasnoyarsk Krai), i.e. not for Lower Chulym proper. Based on field data 2007-2018; the Melet text on the minlang portal marks stress consistently with this rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog 5.1 chul1246 = Lower Chulym (Chibi, Ketsik, Küärik, Yezhi, Yatsi), effectively extinct; Middle Chulym (Tutal, Melet/'Ös') is filed under Shor (tuta1234 'Tutal Middle Chulym', shor1247) in Glottolog 5.1, while ISO 639-3 clw and WALS 'Chulym' (Birjukovich 1997) cover all Chulym varieties. The quoted statement describes the Melet subdialect of Middle Chulym (village Pasechnoe, Tyukhtet district, Krasnoyarsk Krai; speaker A. F. Kondiyakov), not Lower Chulym proper; no stress statement for Lower Chulym itself was reachable (Dul'zon 1952/1966, Birjukovich 1979/1997 not online). Pomorska 2001, the source named by the earlier scan, was opened and is silent on stress.

sources.locator: Part I, Vvedenie, 'Fonologicheskaja sistema glasnykh meletskogo govora srednechulymskogo dialekta', p. 23 (PDF p. 25); repeated verbatim in Tom II p. 8 (PDF p. 10)
sources.note: p. 23 (Melet subdialect of Middle Chulym): word stress on the whole gravitates to the final syllable; in forms with a narrow (high) final vowel it shifts to the preceding broad vowel (parča, parčalarda vs. parčozun, parčalorunda). Intro p. 15 summarises Lower vs Middle Chulym vowel/consonant inventories after Dul'zon, Uraev, Birjukovich, Anderson & Harrison, Li et al., with no stress remark for Lower Chulym.
Neither article says anything about stress; the English phonology section cites Dul'zon 1966, Pomorska 2001 and Li 2008.

sources.citation: Kondiyakov, A. F. & V. M. Lemskaya. 2021. Chulymsko-tjurkskij jazyk d. Pasechnoe... Tom II: Teksty s perevodom i analizom. Tomsk: Izdatel'stvo Tomskogo universiteta. 246 pp.
sources.note: p. 8 repeats the same statement verbatim ("тяготеет к последнему слогу... смещается на предыдущий широкий гласный"), Melet Middle Chulym; texts themselves carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Lemskaya, V. M. (glossed texts) 'Babushka' (Yezhi subdialect of Lower Chulym, D. G. Mamontov, rec. 2010), 'Chulymec i devushka' (Melet, A. F. Kondiyakov), 'Frog' (Tutal, V. M. Gabov) — attachments to the minlang portal page
sources.note: Primary text data, not a description. The Lower Chulym (Yezhi) glossed text carries no stress marks; the Melet plain text marks stress with acute accents (ке́лип, кӧре́лип, са́рығ, ӱзӱне́лип), consistent with the Kondiyakov & Lemskaya rule (stress retracted off high final vowels).

sources.citation: Institute of Linguistics RAS, portal 'Malye jazyki Rossii': Chulymsko-tjurkskij jazyk (page compiled with V. M. Lemskaya), read 2026-09-17
sources.note: Phonetics paragraph gives only inventory counts (8 long / 7-8 short vowels, 6 diphthongs in Lower Chulym, 11-12 consonants); no stress statement. Bibliography of record lists Birjukovich 1979/1984/1979-81/1980/1997, Dul'zon 1966, Lemskaya 2010/2016, Harrison & Anderson 2003/2006/2017, Li et al. 2008, Pomorska 2004/2017.

sources.citation: Pomorska, Marzanna. 2001. The Chulyms and their language. An attempt at a description of Chulym phonetics and nominal morphology. Türk Dilleri Araştırmaları 11: 75-123.
sources.note: Section 5 Phonology (5.1 Vowels pp. 83-89, 5.2-5.3 Consonants pp. 89-97) treats the 8-vowel system, long vowels, reduced vowels, diphthongs, harmony and consonants of Küerik, Lower and Middle Chulym; it says nothing about stress or accent (grep for stress/accent/Betonung: 0 hits). Its reference list identifies Birjukovich 1979 'Zvukovoj stroj čulymsko-tjurkskogo jazyka' (ZS) as the phonology monograph and Menges 1955 (CAJ 1) as the South-Siberian phonology survey.
